item.title: AMD’s Threadripper Halo Station & Ryzen AI MAX PCs Take The Spotlight at IFA, As They Bring Powerful & Local AI Capabilities Close To Everyone
item.description:
AMD presented its most powerful AI solutions for local developers and professionals: the Threadripper Halo Station & various Ryzen AI MAX PCs.

Here's How AMD's Threadripper Halo Station Stacks Up Against NVIDIA's DGX Station, Bringing The World's Most Powerful AI Capabilities In A Desktop Form Factor

The demand for fast local AI is increasing tenfold. As models become larger & agents see huge popularity among the AI masses, the need for powerful hardware is growing at an exponential scale. This demand requires solutions with powerful hardware, and AMD is rolling out its most powerful AI system to date, the Threadripper Halo Station.

Threadripper Halo Station isn't just a regular Threadripper workstation PC; it takes the best of AMD's PRO tier hardware and packs it inside a single box, which AMD calls the "Ultimate Personal AI Workstation".

Starting with the specifications, the AMD Threadripper Halo Station uses the company's fastest Threadripper CPUs such as the Threadripper PRO 9995WX with up to 96 "Zen 5" cores, a total of 192 threads, up to 5.4 GHz clocks, and a huge 384 MB cache. That's lots of CPU horsepower that will be available to end users.

A fast CPU is essential for Agentic AI workflows, but GPUs are just as important. To meet the AI inference demand, the system packs two AMD Instinct workstation GPUs. These are the latest MI350P GPUs , which feature 144 GB of HBM3e memory per card. The system can stack up to four of these cards for an absolutely massive 576 GB of HBM3e memory. Combined, these GPUs will be able to offer up to 16 TB/s of memory bandwidth.

Additionally, the system itself will be able to support large amounts of standard DDR5 memory in the form of RDIMMs. The system packs up to 2 TB of RDIMM memory, pushing the total memory footprint to 2.6 TB, and the total system memory bandwidth to 16.4 TB/s. HBM provides the fast bandwidth while RDIMM provides the capacity.

The whole system comes with a fully liquid-cooled design and will come enclosed in a regular E-ATX chassis with an AMD logo in the front and that Halo aesthetic which the company integrated in its Ryzen AI Halo Mini PCs . The result is massive savings from running AI locally rather than spending large amounts on cloud AI subscriptions.

The Threadripper Halo Station will be able to handle trillion-parameter models and will be launching in 2027. The benefit of AMD's solution is that it features components that are easily acquirable and replicable, giving users options to mix-match or replace the internals to their needs.

And of course, we have to mention how the system compares to its competitor. The AMD Threadripper Halo Station is directly positioned against the NVIDIA DGX Station .

Looking at the comparison between the Threadripper Halo Station and the DGX Station, the AMD solution has more cores and threads on the CPU side. Zen 5 offers fantastic efficiency & is great in terms of IPC, so that equates to stronger single-core performance, & multi-core performance will be speedy too with those 192 threads.

On the memory front, NVIDIA's GB300 does pack more HBM memory on a single chip, but AMD stacks it up to 576 GB using four accelerator cards. NVIDIA also gives users the option to upgrade the capabilities with dedicated AICs such as its flagship 96 GB RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell that gets you another 192 GB of memory. This is GDDR7 memory, which is slower in terms of bandwidth versus AMD's HBM3e solution onboard its MI350P, and the Instinct GPU also packs 50% higher capacities. The overall memory pool is larger on AMD's solution than NVIDIA's.

The pricing remains a constant that is yet to be determined for the Threadripper Halo Station, but AMD has a history of making sure its products are priced very competitively. A DGX Station costs close to $100,000 US, so we can expect AMD to either match or offer its Station at a lower price point, though they don't have to, given the advantages for their solution are ample.

Ryzen AI MAX 400 - MAXING Out Local AI In Portable PCs

In addition to the Threadripper Halo Station, AMD and its partners showcased a strong suite of Ryzen AI MAX 400 PCs at IFA.

Full AMD IFA announcements are listed as below:

  • AMD Ryzen AI Halo systems will support Microsoft’s Project Zenith out of the box , bringing a new Windows developer experience optimized for high-performance devices, coming preinstalled with Visual Studio Code, WSL, GitHub Copilot CLI and PowerShell to help streamline local AI development.
  • AMD Threadripper Halo Station , a prototype system developed that brings datacenter-class AI compute to desk workstation. Combining a Ryzen Threadripper PRO 9995WX with dual Instinct-class accelerators, it lets developers train, fine-tune, and run massive AI models locally without cloud bottlenecks.
  • AMD and SUSE announced a collaboration to help developers move AI applications from local development and testing on AMD Ryzen AI Halo into secure, supported enterprise production environments at scale.

AMD itself went on to showcase some performance aspects of its next-gen Ryzen AI Halo system with the Ryzen AI MAX+ 495 chip and up to 192 GB of unified memory. The system was able to run GLM-5.3 Flash, a 320B parameter model locally, with 58 TPS throughput.

That's impressive because you'd have to spend roughly 500 Euros (cost per ten million output tokens) on Claude Fable 5, a subscription-based AI model, but with Ryzen AI MAX 400 chips, you get the same AI capabilities locally, reducing your AI bill to zero.

AMD's partners such as HP, Lenovo, GMKtec, Acer, Minisforum , Geekom, ACEMAGIC , and several others displayed their latest Ryzen AI MAX laptops and Mini PCs at the event. These will be upgraded to the newer Ryzen AI MAX 400 platform soon, so expect more powerful and local AI capabilities near you, soon.

item.title: OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra Spawns Armies Of Agents That Run On Local CPUs, Handing Intel And AMD A Demand Windfall
item.description:
While OpenAI has yet to open the proverbial floodgates for its latest GPT-6 Astra AI model, initial impressions that are surfacing on the social media suggest the model has a proclivity for spawning a large number of agents, which then strengthens the overarching agent orchestration theme and the attendant demand for more CPUs.

OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra marks a shift from chatbot-style LLMs to a full-fledged computer operator, replete with agents that interact with computers exactly like humans do

We noted earlier this week that OpenAI has now released its latest GPT-6 Astra model to select clients. The model marks a step-change in how LLMs typically operate, with OpenAI taking pains to note that, with Astra, users won't ever have to click around a mouse or type on a keyboard ever again.

Critically, instead of requiring developers to furnish dedicated APIs for every application an AI agent needs to use, GPT-6 Astra is able to navigate any given software in a manner that is strikingly similar to how humans do so: by spawning agents that then work across browsers, spreadsheets, websites and desktop applications, producing finished documents and presentations, and implementing multistep workflows rather than merely telling a user how to complete them.

Basically, GPT-6 Astra's core reasoning engine utilizes a native multi-agent structure to solve complex problems. When faced with a complex task, the model's main orchestration agent can formulate a theory and deploy distinct sub-agents to test variations and validate results in parallel. This native delegation makes it highly resilient against "doom loops" - where model get stuck in repetitive error cycles - allowing it to autonomously debug its own code and adjust its strategy on the fly.

This brings us to the core of today's topic. While the core of GPT-6 Astra runs on the cloud, the model's role as a native computer operator creates a heavy computing loop right on your local device, shifting the load to host CPUs for three major reasons:

  1. Given OpenAI's emphasis on GPT-6 Astra's ability to autonomously discover and chain exploits, enterprises will likely deploy the model within strict isolated local virtual environments, sandboxes, and secure containers (like Docker or MicroVMs), with the spawning, maintaining, and tearing down of these isolated container instances on the fly constituting a highly CPU-intensive process.
  2. To feed Astra proprietary data, enterprises will have to run a harness or orchestration code on local machines, which is again CPU-intensive.
  3. When Astra spawns sub-agents to test variations in parallel or debug a software engineering script locally, your local CPU has to run those test suites. If Astra decides to execute a suite of unit tests, compile code, or rapidly refresh browser processes to verify a workflow, your local CPU handles the brunt of that execution workload.

All of this means that the demand for CPUs is set to sky-rocket, which should bode well for the likes of Intel and AMD.

Do note as well that OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra partially conceals its chain of thought, which should make its distillation a herculean task. This should then make it all the more difficult for China's open-weight AI models to catch up, at least in theory.

Meanwhile, we continue to receive worrying tidbits about a recent incident where as many as 3,700 agents might have colluded autonomously to hack Hugging Face, raising the stakes for cyber security. Basically, these agents colluded to bypass sandbox restrictions and shared the results of their efforts with each other, including by sending "lookahead parties."

item.title: Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 Pro Live Chipset Die Leak Shows A Massive SoC Thanks To The New Heatsink Implementation That’s Meant To Cool The DRAM Effectively
item.description:
The first design glimpse of Qualcomm’s upcoming flagship SoC, the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 Pro , revealed that the chipset has a Heat Pass Block similar to Samsung’s Exynos 2600. Now, we get to see this solution live because a real-life chipset die has been pictured, showing a significantly bigger area than the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 , indicating that we could bear witness to exceptional thermals in the future.

Snapdragon is finally prioritizing thermals with the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 Pro, with a new cooling solution

The traditional PoP (Package-on-Package) implementation is expected to be retired with the arrival of the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 Pro, as @LaidBackDev_ has shared an image showing that the silicon will no longer feature DRAM stacked on top of the SoC die, but it’ll be placed on the side and cooled using a heatsink for maximum dissipation. At first glance, it appears as if the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 Pro’s area will be enormous.

However, that’s only because of the new design change, which we appreciate, but that’ll mean Qualcomm smartphone partners now have to re-engineer the insides of their devices to ensure that there are no compromises on the logic board. The designation number “SM8975” and “101-BC” is also mentioned, indicating that this variant will offer LPDDR5X RAM support instead of the faster and more efficient LPDDR6 memory

With the DRAM now placed on the side and cooled using a heatsink, the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 Pro will now have increased breathing room to hit higher sustained clock speeds on both the CPU and GPU, resulting in improved performance over time rather than just obtaining records for benchmarks that run for a few minutes. We also expect that leveraging TSMC’s new 2nm “N2P” architecture will also come in handy in reducing overall power draw, though we’ll know for sure once the first benchmarks are here.

News Source: @LaidBackDev_

item.title: The Smallest RTX 3060 Spotted With Single Slot Design And No Power Connector Gets Beaten By GTX 1060
item.description:
A weird design for the RTX 3060 was spotted in a Bilibili video, showcasing a single-slot card that only pulls power from the PCIe slot.

Extremely Small RTX 3060 12 GB Surfaces Online, Featuring No Power Connector; Delivers Half the Performance vs a Regular RTX 3060

Someone in China is making ultra-compact GPUs, and we just discovered the smallest GeForce RTX 3060 GPU yet. The video uploaded on Bilibili showcases a navy blue GeForce RTX 3060 card that is hardly equal to the size of a smartphone. The GPU boasts a single-slot form factor and a blower-style cooler. This particular GPU is a low-profile card that appears to be compromised in various ways.

It boasts just two display output connectors, including 1x HDMI and 1x DP, and the surprising part is that it doesn't have even a single external power connector. Meaning this card won't get power except through the PCIe slot, essentially limiting it to a lower power budget (RTX 3060 can be power-limited down to 100W from 170W, but not to 75W without modification). The video uploader assumes that the maker of this card has used shunt modding to alter the power-sensing circuit so that the GPU can operate without a power connector.

By modifying the power-sensing resistor near the PCIe interface, the card appears to have been configured for a lower power target, allowing it to operate within the PCIe slot's limited power budget. Even though GPU-Z reports nearly 145W Board Power Draw and 176W GPU Chip Power Draw, this shouldn't be taken as the card's actual power consumption, as the modification has altered the power-sensing circuitry.

Nonetheless, we can immediately see the effects of it being limited to the power from the PCIe slot, as it can hardly sustain the core clock beyond 900 MHz, while it boasts a boost clock of around 1777 MHz. In 3DMark Time Spy, the card only delivered 4821 points, while a regular RTX 3060 can easily touch 9000 or more. For reference, the score is even lower than the scores generated by the GeForce GTX 1060 and Radeon RX 580, which are ancient budget GPUs.

The card was also reaching 90+ Degrees Celsius on the hotspot, as the cooler wasn't sufficient for adequate cooling. Overall, this GPU was severely throttled in performance as a result of its cooling solution and restricted power delivery, but it might serve as a good alternative for ultra-compact form-factor PCs where there are space constraints and there are no external power connectors available for the GPU.

News Sources: Bilibili , @unikoshardware

item.title: GTA 6
item.description:
Grand Theft Auto 6 , or GTA 6 for short, is quite simply the most anticipated (and most expensive, in all likelihood) product in the history of entertainment. It follows Grand Theft Auto 5 , the second-best-selling game of all time (by verified sales figures) with 225 million units sold , after a 13-year wait that spanned nearly two full console generations.

The industry and gaming fanbase are literally waiting with bated breath to see what developer Rockstar Games has created after such a long development time and such an incredible amount of resources invested in the project. Rockstar North alone spent nearly $3 billion just in staff costs between 2019 and 2025.

Following the Extended Look that premiered on Netflix on Thursday, August 27 , at 3 PM Eastern Time , we have finally uncovered many details about the game and updated our roundup accordingly.

  • Release Date, Platforms, Pricing
  • Genre, Setting, Protagonists
  • Gameplay Features and Mechanics
  • Tech and Specs
  • Sales

Release Date, Platforms, Pricing

Preliminary work on the game started all the way back in 2014, after the launch of GTA 5, but actual development didn't begin until late 2018, following the launch of Red Dead Redemption 2 . Following a long string of rumors, Rockstar Games published the first GTA 6 trailer on December 4, 2023 , as a celebration of the studio's 25th anniversary. The trailer broke the record for the most views on a non-music YouTube video in the first 12 hours, with 46 million views, and within 24 hours, it became the third most viewed video of all time with 93 million views, trailing only two music videos from Korean boy band BTS.

The debut trailer included a 2025 release window, but in May 2025, the studio pushed it to May 26, 2026 . Six months later, Rockstar delayed it again to its current target of November 19, 2026 . Each delay was accompanied by a brief Rockstar statement citing the need for additional polish time, and the second delay sent Take-Two's stock down as much as 18% on the day of announcement. In February 2026, Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick confirmed the November 19 date remains on track and that the marketing campaign will begin in Summer 2026 .

As with its predecessors since GTA 3, the game launches on consoles first, specifically PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series S|X . A PC version has not been officially confirmed , though the series' track record shows it is absolutely on the way. Based on the usual GTA cadence, a PC release in late 2027 or early 2028 would be a reasonable expectation; however, a recent rumor suggests that GTA 6 may be quicker to land on PC than its predecessors .

Official Pricing

In August 2025, Wedbush Securities analyst Michael Pachter predicted that Grand Theft Auto 6 could be the first $100 game , but speaking to Wccftech, analyst Rhys Elliott said it would be a bad idea and predicted a regular $70-$80 price point.

He turned out to be right: Rockstar has now announced that the game's Standard Edition will cost $80 , while an Ultimate Edition is priced at $100 . Pre-orders of both editions include the Vintage Vice City Pack , which comes with the following in-game items:

  • A ’55 Vapid Stanier sedan.
  • Shore Court Garage near Ocean Beach, with a weapon locker and a place to fence stolen goods.
  • Outfits and hairstyles for both Jason and Lucia.
  • An exclusive weapon pattern inspired by Tommy Vercetti’s tropical shirt style.

Pre-ordering GTA 6 from digital stores (the PlayStation Store or Microsoft Store) also grants a complimentary month of GTA+. The GTA+ benefits include:

  • A monthly deposit of GTA$500,000 .
  • Exclusive access to special Shark Cards that provide a 15% bonus in GTA$.
  • Free and discounted vehicles for GTA Online .
  • A changing selection of Rockstar games and featured games.

The more expensive Ultimate Edition includes an exclusive assortment of high-end vehicles, weapons, clothing, and other narrative-related content for Jason and Lucia as they advance through the game:

  • '67 Vapid Dominator Buggy and Paradise Garage : an off-road Mud Club vehicle located in Watson Bay, featuring a weapon locker and stash box.
  • ’95 Grotti Cheetah : a mid-'90s sports car adorned with a retro-futuristic design.
  • Jason's Safehouse vehicle enhancements : a Dinka Enduro motorcycle, Crest Kayak, and a customized Vapid Ganado pickup equipped with a cab spoiler, rear aerials, and unique livery.
  • Vehicle Mod Shops : two exclusive customization hubs, Rideout Customs in Vice City and One-Eyed Willie’s in Lake Leonida.
  • Classic Car Collection : a Wyman commission to refurbish abandoned and project vehicles, including four cars exclusive to the Ultimate Edition.
  • Shitzu Squalo : a pink-and-blue boat stationed at Washington Beach, complete with an explosives-laden weapons crate.
  • Hawk & Little Morgan Revolver : matching versions for Jason and Lucia, featuring Vice City aesthetics.
  • Personalized weapon variants : tailored for Jason’s Girardi ES9 and Lucia’s Klose K17.
  • PTT Youngin$ compound and scores : raid a gang-run illegal goods store in Southside Vice City.
  • Vice City styles for Jason and Lucia : including outfits, tattoos, and more.
  • Goodtime Gear : clothing inspired by Macca the Gator.
  • Stock 305 Clothing Store : an exclusive streetwear boutique.
  • Sara's Unisex Salon : offering hairstyles, facial hair, makeup, and nail services.
  • Electric Fang Tattoo : over 50 unique tattoos crafted by FAILE.

These bonuses will unlock progressively as the protagonists, Jason and Lucia, navigate the story. An Ultimate Edition Upgrade will be available for purchase separately for Standard Edition owners at any time.

Pre-orders for both editions of GTA 6 began at midnight local time on Thursday, June 25 . The physical edition comes only with a digital code , not a disc, which sparked significant controversy.

Genre, Setting, Protagonists

GTA 6 returns to Vice City , Rockstar's fictional analog of Miami, for the first time since the 2002 original. The city now sits within the broader state of Leonida , Rockstar's version of Florida, and the full map is believed to encompass significantly more territory than GTA V's Los Santos and Blaine County combined. Community mapping projects using leaked coordinate data estimate the landmass at over 2 times the size of GTA V's map . Rockstar's official website confirms multiple distinct regions:

  • Vice City — the primary urban environment, modeled on Miami with waterways, Art Deco architecture, high-rises, and the iconic beachfront
  • Leonida Keys — a chain of island communities south of Vice City, where the game's story begins
  • Grassrivers — Rockstar's version of the Everglades, featuring swamps and subtropical wilderness
  • Port Gellhorn — a working port and industrial area
  • Ambrosia — a confirmed additional locale
  • Mount Kalaga National Park — a mountainous natural region in the north of the map

Unlike Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, this game is set in the modern day and leans heavily into the social-media-saturated, influencer-driven culture of contemporary Florida. Both official trailers establish a tone that mixes the criminal underworld of the franchise's roots with a satirical portrait of typical 2020s American excesses, such as tourists recording crime scenes on smartphones, OnlyFans-inspired characters, and sprawling luxury real estate sitting right alongside poverty-stricken trailers.

GTA 6 features two playable protagonists for the first time in a mainline entry. According to Rockstar, when an easy score goes wrong, Jason and Lucia find themselves "on the darkest side of the sunniest place in America, in the middle of a criminal conspiracy stretching across the state of Leonida — forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive." Their story appears to draw clear parallels with Bonnie and Clyde , two world-renowned criminals whose relationship and shared fate drive the narrative. Like them, they are romantically involved.

Jason Duval grew up around grifters and crooks, and after a stint in the Army spent trying to shake off a troubled adolescence, ended up in the Leonida Keys doing what he knows best: running errands for the local drug trade. His landlord, Brian Heder, lets him live rent-free at one of his properties in exchange for help with local shakedowns. Jason's official bio describes him as someone who wants an easy life, but things just keep getting harder.

Lucia Caminos is Rockstar's first female lead in the GTA series. Her father taught her to fight from an early age, and a life of fighting for her family ultimately landed her in Leonida Penitentiary. She enters the story fresh out of prison and determined to only make smart moves going forward, with a life alongside Jason representing her potential way out.

Supporting Cast

The official GTA 6 website reveals a colorful ensemble of side characters orbiting Jason and Lucia:

Real Dimez — Childhood friends Bae-Luxe and Roxy, who parlayed their street savvy into viral rap tracks and a relentless social media presence. After an early hit with local rapper DWNPLY, they're now signed to Only Raw Records, hoping to recapture that momentum.

Brian Heder — Jason's landlord and employer, a veteran drug runner from the golden age of Keys smuggling who still moves product through his boat yard with his third wife, Lori. Rockstar describes him as someone who looks like a Leonida beach bum, but moves like a great white shark.

Cal Hampton — Jason's friend and fellow associate of Brian's, a paranoid homebody who spends his days snooping on Coast Guard comms. Rockstar's description frames him as "at the low tide of America and happy there".

Raul Bautista — A seasoned, charming bank robber always hunting for talent willing to take the biggest risks. His recklessness is apparently a ticking clock: sooner or later, his crew will have to double down or pull their chips from the table.

Boobie Ike — A Vice City legend who transformed street life into a legitimate empire spanning real estate, a strip club, and a recording studio. His current passion project is a partnership with young music mogul Dre'Quan Priest and his fledgling label, Only Raw Records.

Dre'Quan Priest — Always more hustler than gangster, Dre'Quan dealt on the streets to fund his real ambition: breaking into the music industry. He's recently signed Real Dimez , a duo he hopes will put Only Raw Records on the Vice City map.

Gameplay Features and Mechanics

This section previously mentioned possible gameplay details based on the infamous 2022 leak, but now we have Rockstar's 26-minute Extended Look , released originally via Netflix on August 27, 2026 ( with record viewership numbers ), which finally offered the first officially sanctioned look at GTA 6's core systems running on a base PS5:

  • The footage confirms that character switching works on two levels : when Jason and Lucia are together, players can swap between them instantly, for example driving as one while the other rides shotgun, whereas switching while the pair are separated triggers a brief GTA 5-style transition.
  • Combat has been overhauled around manual aiming with aim assist rather than the series' traditional auto-lock, layered with cover-based mechanics that let both protagonists duck behind furniture, vault over car hoods, and swap shoulders to break an enemy's line of sight. The standout new addition is a Dead Eye-inspired bullet-time mode , activated via a purple meter beneath the health bar, that slows combat to a crawl and highlights vulnerable points on enemies, such as the head, hands, and joints, for precision takedowns.
  • The six-star Wanted system , absent since GTA 5 capped out at five, makes a confirmed return, and police AI now factors in a player's clothing, facial appearance, and vehicle when tracking them , meaning a simple change of outfit, a swapped car, or a bandana pulled over the face can genuinely throw off pursuers rather than just outrunning them.
  • Car theft has also been diversified into a choice between a noisy physical struggle, smashing a window, reaching in to unlock the door, and hauling out a resisting driver, or a quieter Slim Jim technique that pops the lock without breaking glass.
  • Rockstar additionally confirmed a physique and lifestyle simulation layer: working out visibly builds muscle over time, poor diet and binge eating add weight, and prolonged sleep deprivation or chaotic living can alter both a character's stats, such as stamina, and their facial appearance.
  • Side content shown or implied in the footage includes basketball, scuba diving, jet skiing, kayaking, wrestling, an in-game shooting range, and competitive racing on dedicated tracks for both cars and bikes , as well as a three-tier robbery system that appears to let players hold up virtually any store in Leonida.

Separately from the Extended Look, in an interview with a French website, Rockstar's Head of Development Rob Nelson confirmed that Vice City is twice as large as GTA 5's Los Santos , and there are eleven times as many little towns as in the previous franchise installment.

We also learned that a campaign playthrough could take up to 80 hours , while a first-person mode won't be available at launch .

GTA 6 Online

Grand Theft Auto 5 may have sold 225 million units, but the real cash cow was GTA Online , whose microtransactions are believed to have brought in between $2.5 and $3 billion . The online mode of the new installment is therefore assured to be a central focus of the studio.

The last patent listed above shows that Rockstar is aiming to deliver a persistent world by minimizing disruptions like session joining as much as possible. This points toward an MMO-like experience , which is exactly what industry veteran Rich Vogel has heard through the grapevine and relayed to Wccftech in an exclusive interview . It also makes perfect sense in light of Rockstar's previous investment in Cfx.re , the company behind the popular roleplaying FiveM modding platform. Earlier this year, Rockstar even launched the Cfx Marketplace , an official modding store for FiveM and Red Dead Online's RedM .

Content creator HipHopGamer has also claimed that GTA 6 will " produce millionaires " with its user-generated content system, though that, too, remains unconfirmed.

Tech and Specs

GTA 6 runs on Rockstar's proprietary RAGE engine (Rockstar Advanced Game Engine), the same technology that underpinned GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2, though substantially evolved over the past decade. The engine's use of patent-backed techniques, including the dynamic LOD system, the locomotion blending architecture, and the NPC navigation model, suggests a renderer designed to sustain an extraordinary density of simulated characters and objects across a world significantly larger than anything Rockstar has previously shipped.

No official technical specification breakdown, be it resolution targets, frame rate modes, or graphics feature list, has been published by Rockstar yet. Given the studio's history, a detailed breakdown of performance modes is expected to be released not long before the game's release.

The 2022 leaked footage showed an early build running at what appeared to be 30 frames per second on console development hardware, consistent with Rockstar's typical approach for its flagship titles. A Performance mode targeting 60 frames per second is something all fans are hoping for, but based on Digital Foundry's early analysis of the trailers, it appears unlikely. Indeed, the trailer footage was confirmed to have been captured on a standard PS5, targeting 1440p at 30fps .

The core reason is ray tracing: Digital Foundry identified pervasive Ray Traced Global Illumination ( RTGI ) throughout the trailer and, crucially, noted that it appears inseparable from the game's artistic vision, not merely a technical flourish. The game also employs real-time ray-traced reflections, which look particularly impressive on glass, plastic, and water surfaces, though it uses a hybrid approach combining RT with Screen Space Reflections (SSR) for performance reasons on larger bodies of water. Shadows, notably, do not look ray-traced; the developer appears to be using filtered shadow maps similar to Red Dead Redemption 2.

Xbox Series S owners should temper their expectations considerably, as the console's RAM limitation (just 8 GB) is likely to force significant compromises, potentially dropping to 720p resolution with ray tracing severely scaled back or disabled entirely, a particularly painful trade-off given how deeply baked into the game's visual identity RT appears to be.

On the opposite end of the spectrum, the game will undoubtedly play best on the world's most powerful console, the PlayStation 5 Pro, as previously suggested in this Wccftech op-ed . That will be even more true if the game supports the upgraded PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) upscaler .

Sales

Given the behemoth that is GTA 6, analysts are eager to predict what kind of sales the game will be able to pull off. According to preliminary Newzoo data, the pre-order campaign has generated around $260 million globally in the first week. The analytics firm then used a model to predict up to 51 million units sold by the end of the game's launch week, generating roughly $5.2 billion in revenue. Earlier, Piper Sandler estimated that GTA 6 could sell over 45 million units on its launch day .

item.title: Insider Claims Insomniac Is Still Working on the Leaked Standalone Marvel’s Venom Game, but No-One Knows When It’ll Be Unveiled
item.description:
How We Rate Rumors
  • 0-20%: Unlikely - Lacks credible sources
  • 21-40%: Questionable - Some concerns remain

Insomniac Games is about to launch Marvel's Wolverine , but the studio's massive leak from December 2023 also revealed that they have been working on a standalone Venom game for quite some time. Still, with no official announcement of the project, fans are wondering whether it's still happening.

According to insider Nate the Hate , that's absolutely the case:

Venom is very much still in development, upon last check. As to when it'll be announced, I don't know.

Let's take a step back and look at what we know from previous leaks and rumors, then. The December 2023 leak was caused by a Rhysida ransomware attack that put roughly 1.3 million Insomniac files into circulation. Buried among them was a highly detailed studio roadmap, and Venom sat right at the front of it . The leaked slate had Venom arriving in 2025 , followed by Wolverine in 2026, Spider-Man 3 in 2028, a new Ratchet & Clank in 2029, and an X-Men game in 2030, with unannounced new IP roughly planned for the early and mid-2030s.

The game's full title, per the leaked material, was going to be Venom: Lethal Protector , borrowing from the 1993 comic run that gave the character his best-known nickname. The project slides described it as continuing directly from Spider-Man 2 (which, as those who have already played it know, prominently featured Venom) and leading into Spider-Man 3.

The leaked internal documentation even revealed a planned budget of $120 million , far smaller than the $300 million spent on Spider-Man 2, suggesting a shorter experience more akin to Spider-Man: Miles Morales . Indeed, the leak also included information on the game's scope: a roughly 8-to-10-hour campaign centered on 12 main missions, with optional content such as bases, crimes, and collectibles.

Following the late 2023 leak, the next big rumor came last year from MP1st , which confirmed that Marvel's Wolverine was on track to launch in 2026 and also that Marvel's Venom was still in development, with sources indicating Eddie Brock would be the symbiote's host rather than Harry Osborn , and that this Venom would look considerably closer to his comic incarnation.

A few months ago, fans got a bit of a scare when Miles Morales actor Nadji Jeter suggested that the project had been canceled following the premature death of Tony Todd (who had voiced the character in Marvel's Spider-Man 2), but Bloomberg's Jason Schreier quickly disputed that claim , reassuring gamers that the standalone Venom game was still being made.

Nate the Hate's latest confirmation is yet another hint that we will eventually get to play this game. When, though, is a more complicated matter . The leaked Insomniac Games schedule tells us it was supposed to launch ahead of Wolverine, but it's clearly been postponed. Late next year makes sense, but that slot in Sony's first-party release calendar might be taken by Naughty Dog's Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet . Still, given that this might be a medium-sized game based on available info, it's not inconceivable that both might launch in Fall 2027.

item.title: Blizzard’s StarCraft Site Breaks Itself Days Before BlizzCon, and Fans Already Decoded a Hidden 2575 Horror ARG
item.description:
With BlizzCon 2026 kicking off in just over a week in Anaheim, Blizzard 's official StarCraft website has started behaving strangely , and the community has wasted no time picking its not-at-all-casual glitches apart. What began as a handful of glitch effects on the StarCraft Remastered page now looks like a full-blown alternate reality game, with hidden logs, transmissions, and manifests buried in the site's code pointing toward something new brewing in the Koprulu Sector.

Inspecting the site's dev tools reveals a string of decrypted ASCII transmissions dated August–September 2575 , which would be a 67-year jump forward from the end of StarCraft II: Legacy of the Void (the third and final expansion to StarCraft II), whose events ended in 2508 according to the official timeline.

The messages are addressed to the Aokara Lunar Mining Complex on a planet called Roxara , a location lore experts will recognize from the Dominion bioweapon backstory and old StarCraft: Ghost material, most notably its appearance in the Frontline comic Fear the Reaper . A Terran military unit dubbed Theta Squadron is shown en route via freighter to dock at the complex, hauling heavy equipment, autocannons, electronics, and "confidential research crates" under strict security protocols labeled Special Order 176 and Special Order 132 .

The station's sensor telemetry also shows power grid fluctuations, zero registered living occupants, but 14 unidentified motion signatures . Medical data layered into the logs reportedly shows erratic pulse rates, breached security clearances, and flagged accounts, the kind of horror-adjacent detail that has fans speculating about an infestation or containment breach scenario. At least eight separate ARG messages have been cataloged so far.

Three main theories out of a very loud rumor mill

The StarCraft community has largely converged on three possibilities for what the ARG is actually teasing:

  • A cooperative tactical extraction or horde shooter built around Theta Squadron's arrival at a compromised facility.
  • A revival of the long-dead StarCraft: Ghost concept, leaning into the covert-ops, bioweapon-containment angle that Roxara's lore seems a great fit for.
  • A broader single-player story campaign that simply uses this ARG as a framing device for a new StarCraft narrative-driven entry.

Adding fuel to the fire, BlizzCon 2026's official schedule contains a conspicuous hour-long gap on the main stage between the first big WoW panel and the Diablo developer update. The timing has fed speculation that the slot is being held open for this StarCraft reveal. Unverified leaks have also circulated referencing a panel called "StarCraft Infantry: Deep Dive," though outlets have been careful to label that specific title as unconfirmed and possibly fabricated.

All signs have long pointed to something new happening for this franchise at BlizzCon 2026 . A StarCraft shooter has been rumored since journalist Jason Schreier first reported on its existence in 2024 , reportedly helmed by Dan Hay , the former executive director of Ubisoft's Far Cry series, alongside a design director with credits at Insomniac and The Coalition.

Later reporting described the project as a gritty, Unreal Engine-powered AAA shooter that ditches Overwatch's stylized look for something closer to StarCraft II's cinematic tone, built around squad-based PvE combat, vehicle sections, and large boss encounters, a very different pitch than the long-dead Ghost project.

Where Nexon fits into all this

The ARG timing lines up with a separate thread of StarCraft rumors out of South Korea . Earlier coverage revealed that the Korean developer would be making the next game in the IP, and more recent rumors have gone further, claiming that Nexon may be close to acquiring the StarCraft IP outright from Blizzard , potentially paving the way for Nexon's involvement in a mainline sequel like StarCraft III. That creates a genuinely tangled picture heading into BlizzCon : is the ARG teasing Dan Hay's internally developed AAA shooter, a Nexon-driven mainline StarCraft project, some combination of both, or something else entirely?

Blizzard has not officially acknowledged the ARG, confirmed a new StarCraft project, or commented on any of the Nexon rumors. But between the site's deliberate glitching, the timing just ahead of BlizzCon 2026, and years of accumulating rumors about both a shooter and a Korean licensing deal, all signs point to some kind of clarity arriving very soon .

BlizzCon's opening ceremony kicks off on September 12 at 10:30 AM Pacific Time , and if this ARG is what it looks like, fans of the sci-fi franchise won't be waiting long to find out which rumor was closer to the truth.

item.title: Modder Enables DLSS 5 Neural Rendering On AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT; Performance Tanks Significantly, But Latest Version Improves FPS By 12%
item.description:
Someone just got the latest DLSS 5 technology working on AMD RDNA 4 GPUs through a simple executable file.

DLSS NR Now Works on AMD RDNA 4 GPUs as Modder Prepares Executable That Enables it on RX 9070 XT in Some Games

In the last few days, we saw DLSS 5 being implemented in several games unofficially , apart from the official implementation in NBA 2K7 . Modders and enthusiasts were also successful in enabling DLSS 5 Neural Rendering on older GPUs such as the RTX 40 series , RTX 30 series, and RTX 20 series . Even though NVIDIA promised to bring NR to RTX 40 later , it's still being restricted to the RTX 50 series for some time.

Since DLSS 5 Neural Rendering relies on FP8 for its current real-time neural rendering model, there's no reason why it can't run on the latest generation of GPUs. And that raises the question of whether it's possible to enable DLSS 5 NR on AMD RDNA 5 GPUs that boast native hardware support for FP8. Looks like it's possible, and a modder has been successful in enabling the implementation on an RX 9000 series GPU.

Ancient Gameplays uploaded a video, confirming that the modder's workaround works. He demonstrated enabling DLSS 5 NR on his Radeon RX 9070 XT in games like Cyberpunk 2077. The process is pretty straightforward: the " dlssnr_on_amd_setup.exe " file needs to be placed into the bin\x64 folder, such as in games like Cyberpunk 2077. The next step involves getting the " nvngx_dlssnr.dl " file and placing it in the same folder.

Once you run the " dlssnr_on_amd_setup.exe " file, you will have to follow some basic instructions. Then you can run your game and turn on FSR (either FSR 3 or FSR 4). By pressing End for the overlay, you will then need to run the executable file again and choose "update" (U) or "remove" (R) to enable or disable DLSS 5 NR in the game.

As you can see from the video, without DLSS 5 NR, Cyberpunk 2077 was running at 80+ FPS on RX 9070 XT, but as soon as NR was enabled, the FPS dropped to just 11-12. So, DLSS 5 is really costing a lot of performance due to the lack of optimizations, but the modder has released more versions since then, including Alpha v0.2.7, which adds 12% performance, enabling 30 FPS at 1080p in Cyberpunk 2077 . The modder also notes that DLSS 5 also works in GTA V: Enhanced with Radeon RX 9070 XT with the same method.

item.title: Chinese Chip Making Equipment Firm Naura Claims Big Breakthrough That Could Enable CXMT To Overcome EUV Sanctions & Make 3D DRAM Chips
item.description:
China's Naura Technology Group, a key domestic semiconductor manufacturing equipment provider, claims to have developed a two-step etch process for manufacturing 3D DRAM chips. 3D DRAM chips are the next generation of DRAM technology as they seek to overcome the constraints of current chips when it comes to cell density.

A paper published by Naura in the IEEE journal explains progress made in etching uniformly across the 64 layers of 3D DRAM to shift the focus to vertical manufacturing instead of the horizontal constraints encountered by non-EUV lithography.

Chinese Chip Equipment Manufacturer Naura Details Breakthrough In Semiconductor Etch Engineering That Could Help CXMT

As Western sanctions restrict the sales of advanced EUV chip manufacturing machines to China, the country's chip designers are increasingly focused on the vertical aspect of semiconductor fabrication and design. The primary benefit of EUV lithography is that it enables manufacturers and designers to create chips with finer circuit pathways and patterns that spread out horizontally on a piece of silicon.

Earlier this year, Huawei created quite a bit of stir when it announced a new chip design technology called Tau Scaling. At the center of this approach was Huawei's LogicFolding architecture which folds and stacks logic circuits vertically in order to reduce resistance, improve connectivity and even achieve performance and transitory density equivalent to standard 1.4 nanometer chips by 2031. Through these, the need to increase transistor density by reducing circuit sizes through EUV is replaced by focusing on vertical stacking.

Firm Claims Cyclic Two-Step Etch Process Can Improve Depth Uniformity & High Selectivity - Says Uniformity Has Been Achieved "Across 64 Layer Pairs"

Now, research published by China's Naura Technology hints that the country might be taking a similar approach for memory fabrication. In it, the firm describes a method to perform uniform etching on a 64-layer 3D DRAM stack relying on Silicon (Si) and Silicon-Germanium (SiGe) layers. In 3D DRAM design, these two materials are stacked alternatively and the SiGe is removed to make room between the Si layers to lay out the wordiness, bit lines and gates inside what is called a channel floor.

The process of removing these SiGe layers is called etching, and in its research paper, Naura claims to overcome the traditional limitations in the process. These limitations include the etching chemicals 'eating' into the adjacent Si layers to disrupt their uniformity, the by-products of the process settling at the bottom of the stack and the inability of the chemicals to reach the bottom layers as well.

Overcoming them can enable CXMT to progress to 3D DRAM and vertical fabrication in order to overcome the horizontal transistor density constraints faced by DUV equipment.

The aforementioned problems are referred to as low selectivity for the Si layer damage and micro-loading for the bottom contaminant buildup. Overcoming them improves the process's depth uniformity or the size of the gap in the Si-Si layers.

On the etching front, Naura uses a two step process . The first step involves blasting unbiased (electrically neutral) Fluorine radicals in the SiGe layers. This ensures that only the SiGe is targeted by the etching materials, leading to a fine protective film of germanium fluoride forming on the Si layer. The second step is purging the chemical by-products through a plasma-assisted purge step, which removes the micro loading from the process.

According to the company, this process enables it to achieve a Si to SiGe etch selectivity greater than 500 to 1. This rate implies that the SiGe layers are etched more than 500 times faster than the Si layers for a layer between the two Si layers that is 200 nanometers thick.

The loss rate is accompanied by a loss of less than 10 angstroms for the Silicon layer, says the firm. Finally, Naura also claims that the structural uniformity is greater than 95% to imply that the bottom layer is at least 190 nanometers thick if the top layer is 200 nanometers thick "across 64 layer pairs."

item.title: Gaming Laptop’s Excessive Overheating Caused A DDR5 Power Rail Failure, But This Level Of Hardware Problems Is Caused By None Other Than User Neglect
item.description:
The number of powerful components inside a gaming laptop makes them extremely high-maintenance machines, but that’s the trade-off if you want incredible performance that you can take with you. Unfortunately, some users often forget that there’s a ton of care that accompanies owning one of these, and neglecting this pricey hardware can become deleterious in the future. One gaming laptop’s DDR5 power rail blew out because of this reason, and the culprit can be effortlessly spotted.

Clogged fans preventing proper airflow resulted in a gaming laptop’s overheating, causing the DDR5 power rail to fail

A slew of malfunctioning or dead Alienware gaming laptops are shown at @dellpartspeople’s YouTube channel, and in one of his shorts, he reveals that the customer informed him that the machine won’t power on. When the repair expert lifted the bottom cover, he immediately recognized that it was the user’s lack of maintenance of the gaming laptop that resulted in catastrophic failure, as the fans were practically choked.

Without reaching for his multimeter, he recognized that the DDR5 power rail had likely shorted out. Sure enough, his assumption turned out to be true, and without wasting precious time, his first order of business was to replace the blown-out capacitor. Replacing this component was an easy fix, but for others, it can become difficult to diagnose, especially when you lack the experience of @dellpartspeople.

As mentioned above, gaming laptops are extremely prone to overheating, even if they are regularly maintained, so to prevent these machines from becoming expensive paperweights, it’s imperative that users exercise various precautions to extend the lifespan of their ridiculously pricey hardware. They can start by changing the thermal paste for the CPU and GPU, followed by removing the thermal putty or pads on the GPU memory, VRMs, and MOSFETs.

If you’re too nervous to get inside your gaming laptop, we also recommend the good old-fashioned undervolting method. For Intel processors, there’s no better software than ThrottleStop, and if you want to obtain lower temperatures for your graphics processor, there’s no better alternative than MSI Afterburner.

item.description:
It was only in July that DeepSeek's CEO created seismic waves by boldly declaring that NVIDIA was digging its own grave in China . And now, merely weeks later, DeepSeek is apparently helping that prognostication come to fruition by placing a massive order for Huawei's Ascend 950DT AI chips, further dimming NVIDIA's prospects in a market that is increasingly becoming insular.

DeepSeek has reportedly eschewed NVIDIA's China-specific H200 GPUs to place a gigantic ~$2.56 billion order for 160,000 units of Huawei's Ascend 950DT chips, which will populate its new 1GW data center in Mongolia

Bloomberg is now reporting that DeepSeek has placed a massive order of 160,000 Ascend 950DT chips with Huawei to populate its 1GW data center in inner Mongolia. With the street price of each 950DT chip currently hovering at around 111,000 Yuan or ~$16,000 (vs. $15,000 to $25,000 for NVIDIA's H20 GPU), the total order might amount to ~$2.56 billion.

Of course, Huawei's production capacity for the Ascend 950DT chip is extremely constrained at the moment, limited to only a few hundred thousand units per year. This means that Huawei can take as much as 1 year to fulfill DeepSeek's order.

For the benefit of those who might not be aware, the Ascend 950DT chip is built on Huawei's self-developed third-generation DaVinci v3 architecture, and leverages SMIC's N+3 process technology (an advanced 7-nanometer class process).

While the chip can handle both the training- and decode-related workloads, DeepSeek is primarily placing this order to fulfil its inference needs. What's more, each Ascend 950DT chip comes equipped with 144 GB of specialized High Bandwidth Memory (HiZQ 2.0 HBM), achieving a 4.0 TB/s memory bandwidth and a 2.0 TB/s GPU-to-GPU interconnect speed. It also natively supports low-precision formats such as FP8, FP4, and Huawei's proprietary HiF8.

Of course, Huawei also features the chip within its Atlas 950 SuperPoD infrastructure, which links up to 8,192 Ascend 950DT chips to deliver 8 EFLOPS of peak AI compute power.

Do note that DeepSeek's CEO, Liang Wenfeng, had noted back in July that "all tasks [NVIDIA] GB300 can do, the Huawei supernode can do, latency and all the same. The only cost: 4 Huawei GPUs equal 1 NVIDIA GPU, and it's two years behind."

To summarize, DeepSeek has opted to go with Huawei's Ascend 950DT chips instead of NVIDIA's H20 GPUs despite a ~4x performance hit, a year-long delay in delivery, and not-too-hefty of a price differential. Despite not having a particular love for first-person games in general, I had tons of fun when I tried the beginning of the game during last year's gamescom , so much so that I ranked the game as one of the best titles I played during the show, if not the very best.

While I was disappointed by Valor Mortis' delay to October 13 due to September's stacked release schedule, I cherished the opportunity to play the game again before its launch. With gamescom 2026 filled to the brim with high-quality games like Castlevania: Belmont's Curse and Final Fantasy Resonance , the Soulslike by One More Level had a more challenging time ranking as high as it did last year, but ultimately, it still did, as the hands-on session One More Level invited me to only confirmed how Valor Mortis is set to become one of the best Soulslikes of the year.

As opposed to last year's demo, which let me experience the beginning of the game, this year's demo was set a little further on in the adventure. Thrown into a dilapidated village filled with crazed villagers and exploding cows (!), Napoleon had to make his way through fending off all sorts of dangers, armed only with a few weapons, which included a trusty saber, a few guns, and magical powers that let him unleash a powerful fireball, among other things.

Despite the first-person view, Valor Mortis feels unmistakably Soulslike, with stamina dictating how often Napoleon can attack, block, and dodge attacks. Interestingly enough, the single melee attack button can feel a little limiting, but that is not exactly the case, as the variety of combat options are granted by the ranged attacks, which feel more central to the experience than in other Soulslikes.

Like many other similar games, Valor Mortis also features parry mechanics that allow the player to open an enemy up by blocking an attack just before an attack connects. Although this is nothing new for the genre, its implementation in the game is extremely good. Despite the far from optimal play conditions, I had no trouble parrying attacks based only on visual and sound cues, as it felt incredibly intuitive and natural. The parry window is just right, and this was something One More Level Games told me they put great focus on, due to the first-person view of the experience.

Valor Mortis also delivers in terms of level design. Although it wasn't anything overly complex, the village felt intricate enough, with plenty of shortcuts and alternate paths, which also involved some light parkouring to get through, adding more variety to an experience that I believe more and more does everything right.

With two hands-on sessions under my belt, I firmly believe Valor Mortis will become one of the best Soulslikes of the current generation, if not of all time. With tight gameplay and a very unique setting, One More Level is crafting something special that I can't wait to experience in full when it launches on October 13 on PC , PlayStation 5 , Xbox Series X , and Xbox Series S .

item.title: ASUS’ Official Vendors Are Listing NUC PCs With 96GB RAM Models At Incredibly Affordable Prices, But Fail To Mention That Memory Or Storage Aren’t Included To Deceive Buyers
item.description:
The consumer DRAM market is in complete shambles, giving vendors a golden opportunity to resort to questionable tactics to sell their hardware. On this occasion, one customer noticed that official ASUS vendors on Amazon have listed the Taiwanese manufacturer’s NUC PCs at practically throwaway prices when considering that these machines ship with 96GB of DDR5 RAM. However, a closer look reveals that these NUCs don’t ship with any kind of memory or storage.

Listings of ASUS NUC PCs clearly mention 96GB RAM, but customers later find out these are just barebone units

On Amazon Italy, Redditor “TrieMond” stumbled upon a listing where he noticed that official ASUS vendors were selling the NUC 14 PRO for €575.07, or $667.75 when using direct currency conversion. That’s a pretty standard price for a mini PC, until you get to see what's under the hood. From an Intel Core Ultra 7 155H CPU to 96GB RAM operating at 5,600MT/s to an M.2 SSD with an undisclosed storage capacity and other additions.

The problem here isn’t the specifications, but how these sellers are misleading customers into making purchases and not getting what they paid for. For instance, the Redditor mentioned that buyers later found out after they unboxed the NUC 14 PRO that the 96GB RAM and SSD aren’t present in the PC, and these have to be purchased separately. From this listing, there’s no disclaimer like this mentioned, meaning that ASUS’ official vendors are blatantly misleading customers.

If you visit Amazon’s U.S. page, the price of two 48GB 5,600MT/s SODIMM RAM modules from Crucial costs a whopping $1,549 on the online retailer , so it’s clear that the Italian listings are just baiting unsuspecting customers into picking up the NUC 14 PRO. In the age of the DRAM shortage , a mini PC housing 96GB of RAM and going for less than $700 is a steal of a deal. Now, it shouldn’t be surprising that sellers will execute all manner of tactics to ensure that they obtain a hefty number of daily sales, but the fault also lies with Amazon.

The listings shouldn’t mention that these products feature 96GB RAM, and if these machines don’t ship with the aforementioned memory or storage, it should clearly be mentioned. Sure, these NUCs can simply be returned to Amazon in exchange for a refund, but that’s a whole new exercise that customers need to be prepared for, so why not tackle the problem at the source?

News Source: Reddit

item.title: GTA 6 PC Could Arrive Sooner Than Expected, As Rising Console Prices Reportedly Pressure Rockstar to Move Fast
item.description:
How We Rate Rumors
  • 0-20%: Unlikely - Lacks credible sources
  • 21-40%: Questionable - Some concerns remain
  • 41-60%: Plausible - Reasonable evidence
  • 61-80%: Probable - Strong evidence
  • 81-100%: Highly Likely - Multiple reliable sources
RUMOR ASSESSMENT

85%

Highly Likely

Source 5/5

Corroboration 4/5

Technical 4/5

Timeline 4/5

GTA 6 is finally launching on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S in a little over two months, but the wait for PC players will be longer, as Rockstar Games has yet to announce when this version of the game will launch. In the recent past, it took roughly one year for games like GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2 to launch on PC following their PlayStation 4 and Xbox One releases, but there's been some ramblings that the current console market conditions which are forcing the prices of consoles up years after their original launch may push Rockstar Games and Take-Two Interactive to release the sixth entry in the series in less than one year.

"I do think they'll push the PC version up," said VGC 's Andy Robinson during the latest episode of the VGC Podcast during a wider discussion on the impact the high price of gaming hardware is having on the entire industry. "There's a bit of noise about that. That perhaps the PC version might arrive sooner than some people might expect just because of everything that's going on."

Although VGC has an excellent track record, we have to take the possibility of GTA 6 releasing on PC in less than one year after its PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S launch with a grain of salt. Still, this possibility makes a lot of financial sense for a few reasons. For starters, there are many who do not own a current-generation console, but still have a PC that can play games, and with technologies like NVIDIA DLSS and AMD FSR , the game could very well run decently even on somewhat dated machines. In addition, Rockstar Games and Take-Two Interactive could time the launch of GTA 6 to coincide with the release of the next iteration of GTA Online , which would b enefit from increased exposure if it came shortly after a PC launch that will likely be as successful as the console launch.

Still, those who want to experience GTA 6 at its best, and don't want to wait for the inevitable PC version, will only have the option of playing the game on PlayStation 5 Pro . While this version of the game has yet to be fully detailed, a recent leak suggests that Rockstar Games may stick with the base model's 30 FPS and deliver a 4K experience.
